title: Contract on Methods
concept: Methods can have contracts too — requires and ensures that reference self to validate object state before and after method execution.
why: Object-oriented code without contracts leads to invalid object states. Method contracts ensure every operation maintains the object's integrity.
tips: Use self@pre to verify state transitions in methods
Method contracts compose with type invariants — invariant is checked AFTER method's ensures
Methods that only read (&Self) typically only need ensures, not requires
common_mistakes: Forgetting self@pre in ensures for mutable methods
Writing requires that duplicate the type invariant
Modifying self in a &Self (immutable) method — caught by the borrow checker
